\title{Hybrid Retrieval for Indian Equity Filings}

\begin{abstract}
We present a hybrid retrieval system. Studies show that dense retrieval
underperforms on numerical tables.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Sparse retrieval remains competitive on out-of-domain data \citep{thakur2021beir}.
Reciprocal rank fusion improves recall by 12\% over single-retriever baselines.
Prior work demonstrates that cross-encoders add substantial precision.
As shown in Figure 2, our pipeline has three stages.

\section{Methods}
We train BGE-M3 \citep{chen2024bgem3} on 240,000 passages.
We set the learning rate to 2e-5 over 3 epochs.
Our reranker is initialised from \citet{nogueira2019passage}.

\section{Results}
Our system achieves 93\% Recall@1 and 0.967 MRR.
We compare against \citep{robertson2009bm25} and \cite{ghost2030nonexistent}.
Retrieval latency fell by 3.2x relative to the dense-only baseline.
